analysis: Integration of the SSD eviction refactor (T-041, TB-007, A-001). Replayed source shows SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest (new, lines ~11-44): one index.oldest() probe, then retire. It returns 0 on externalChange, which preserves the old reconciliation behavior. It returns freed bytes if any, stops if isClosed(), and otherwise walks a single oldestFirstSnapshot, skipping the first tag. Each attempt re-checks externalChange, freed bytes and isClosed. The pass is bounded by the snapshot size. SSDBlockIndex.OldestFirstSnapshot is a correct min-heap: heapify from count/2-1, pop-last/swap-root/siftDown, and a comparator identical to oldest() (lastAccess, then unsigned-byte lexicographic tag). The copy is made under the index lock and iteration is lock-free, so there is no deadlock with retirement. SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift:13-21 and SSDPrefixCache.evictOldestEntry now guard on !isClosed and delegate. Both still route deletion through retireIndexedEntries, so the removal lock, hasSafeRoot, ownsEvictionRoot, file leases, no-follow unlink and non-rotating epoch semantics are unchanged. The only behavior differences are an added closed-store early exit (a tightening) and victim selection from a snapshot taken after the first attempt, which affects eviction choice only. There is no change to the HMAC naming, AES-GCM/DBK3, the 1800s TTL, KEK purge, salt scoping or the disk-budget policy, so the SEC-035 sign-off triggers are untouched. Docs and changelog accurately match the replayed implementation. The tests are test-only. Residual: the SSDPrefixCache.swift hunk and the test files were not replayed. The old code's per-victim externalChange return is preserved in the helper as seen. Omitted units (41) were not available for replay, so completeness is a coverage limit. No security regression or threat-model update is identified.
